hypotheses.note: any GX.SingularHSStructure; GX.IsSingularHSSurface is not needed to state positivity. Regular HS-surfaces are positive (GX.SingularHSStructure.isPositive_ofHSSurface).
There is no AdS spacetime at this layer, so an interaction x is positive when its HS-sphere Σ_x is (SingularHSStructure.IsPositive applied to Σ_x). See SCOPE (f).

A singular line is positive when its type L is (GammaLinkCircle.IsPositive), since its type is its circle (l.983–984). Through 𝔢(L), only the apex p̄ is handled; the apex −p̄ needs bbsrem:p_p (SCOPE (f)).
points of 𝒮, each through a link at the apex p̄ (IsApexLink, l.782–783). Regular points of 𝒮 are not counted as time-like singularities (IsRegular). See SCOPE (b), (d) and (e).
p ∈ dS² / minkQ p = 0 (∂ℍ²±) / minkQ p < 0 (ℍ²±)
f = δ^k g, g has a fixed point, k ≥ 2. Since k is even (…IsLiftedDev.even_of_nonneg), k ≥ 1 is equivalent; the bridges are stated for 1 ≤ k.

In the form of l.915 (OQ-120 (c)), required for every lifted developing pair with θ oriented and for every decomposition. When g is hyperbolic this is exactly IsSpacelikePositive (isPositive_iff_of_deSitter).
g x ≥ x on ℝP̃¹. When g is parabolic this is exactly IsLightlikePositive (isPositive_iff_of_null).
coneAngle = angle f / 2 (OQ-113 (a)/(b)). It equals 2π at a regular point, and coneAngle < 2π iff f < δ² (coneAngle_lt_two_pi_iff, which needs no normalisation).

findings: l.948–953 with l.1510–1511. The definition of a singular HS-surface (l.948–953) does not require the points of 𝒮 to be singular. 𝔢(ℓ(p)) = HS² (GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.regular_susp) is a valid model, so 𝒮 may contain regular points. A regular point at a time-like p has cone angle exactly 2π (GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsRegular.coneAngle_eq, GX.GammaLinkCircle.coneAngle_regular). Read literally, « all time-like singularities have a cone angle less than 2π » (l.1510–1511) would make every surface whose 𝒮 contains a regular time-like point non-positive. The time-like clause is therefore read for non-regular links only (GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsRegular). Regular links satisfy the two other clauses as printed (GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsRegular.isPositive).

l.906–915. The « in other words » of l.915 (g x ≥ x on I⁺) is not equivalent to the primary form of l.908–913 (left ends of the components of I⁺ are repelling fixed points of g) when the Γ_p-holonomy is trivial. GX.exists_isPositive_delta_four builds such a circle at every p ∈ dS²: a non-regular space-like (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-circle of degree 4 (the 2-fold cyclic cover of ℓ(p), lifted holonomy δ⁴, so g = 1). It is positive in l.915's form, with equality. In l.908–913's form it is neither positive nor negative: it is neither GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsSpacelikePositive nor …IsSpacelikeNegative, since no decomposition has g hyperbolic. Its underlying ℝP¹-circle is not hyperbolic (¬ GTilde.IsHyperbolic δ⁴, in the same theorem). This is the singular counterexample to l.794–795 (« L is a hyperbolic ℝP¹-circle ») that T-bbs-hs-link-types argued but did not build. Causality (Def Hcausal, l.1114) excludes degree ≥ 4, so positive causal surfaces are unaffected.
questions: OQ-113 (a)/(b), the cone angle. The paper never defines the cone angle of a (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-circle (l.804–806, l.863–864). Reading taken: coneAngle C = angle f / 2, where f is the lifted holonomy of any lifted developing pair with θ oriented (it does not depend on the choice, coneAngle_eq). The factor ½ comes from ℓ(p) being developed through the double cover linkCover, one turn being δ². Equivalently, coneAngle = Θ/2 for Θ the real angle of the underlying ℝP¹-circle (« a link's angle is twice the cone angle », coneAngle_eq_half). It is 2π at a regular point. The condition coneAngle < 2π is f < δ² pointwise, which needs no normalisation (coneAngle_lt_two_pi_iff); it is N9's P̃y < δy in the visual lift (GX.SingKind.IsPositive). The mark waits on OQ-113.

OQ-120 (c), the form of positivity. Reading taken: l.915's form, required for every lifted developing pair (θ oriented) and every decomposition f = δ^k g. When g is hyperbolic it equals IsSpacelikePositive, and when g is parabolic it equals IsLightlikePositive (both proved). The two forms differ only for trivial holonomy (finding 2): this reading calls those circles positive. Which form is of record? The mark waits on OQ-120.

« Singularity » in l.1509–1511 (finding 1). Reading taken: a point of 𝒮 whose link is not (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-isomorphic to ℓ(p) (GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsRegular). Only the time-like clause needs this guard. Should l.948–953 require the points of 𝒮 to be singular instead?

Which apex carries the singular point. Reading taken: x ∈ 𝒮 is read at the apex p̄, following l.782–783 (« the singularity corresponding to p has a preferred status »). GX.SingularHSStructure.IsApexLink is an HS-isomorphism (SingularHSStructure.IsIso, OQ-126 (b)) from a neighbourhood of x into 𝔢(L) that sends x to height 0. The strict GX.IsSingularHSSurface allows either apex. The link at −p̄ belongs to bbsrem:p_p (T-bbs-p-p, GX.GammaLinkCircle.antipode in HSAntipodal.lean).

Some link or every link (l.785 « mutually non isomorphic », l.850–853). Reading taken for GX.SingularHSStructure.IsPositive: every point of 𝒮 has some positive link at p̄. GX.SingularHSStructure.IsPositiveEvery is the other reading: every link at p̄ is positive. The two agree if the type of an HS-singularity is well defined, which is not formalized. Proved: IsPositiveEvery together with HasApexLinks implies IsPositive. Positivity is invariant under isomorphisms of circles at the same p (GammaLinkCircle.IsIso.isPositive_iff); invariance under isomorphisms that move p is OQ-120 (a). Which reading is of record?

Singular lines and interactions (l.983–984, l.1117). Reading taken: a singular line is positive when its type L is (GammaLinkCircle.IsPositive), and an interaction is positive when its HS-sphere Σ_x is (SingularHSStructure.IsPositive). By analogy with Def Hcausal (« a singular line is causal if 𝔢(L) is causal », l.1117), a line could instead be read through 𝔢(L). What is proved: if L is positive then p̄ is a positive point of 𝔢(L) (DevData.isPositiveAt_north); if 𝔢(L) is positive in the every-link reading then L is positive (DevData.isPositive_of_isPositiveEvery). Not formalized: « 𝔢(L) is positive iff L is ». It also needs the apex −p̄, i.e. bbsrem:p_p (C.antipode, DevData.isIso_flip) together with « C.antipode is positive iff C is », and the previous question.

kb_proposals: Positivity of an HS-singularity or singular line is GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsPositive, a structure with fields timelike, spacelike and lightlike. The last two use l.915's form for every lifted pair. Bridges: isPositive_iff_of_timelike, isPositive_iff_of_deSitter (IsSpacelikePositive) and isPositive_iff_of_null (IsLightlikePositive).

A positive singular HS-surface is GX.SingularHSStructure.IsPositive: every point of 𝒮 has a positive link at the apex p̄ (IsApexLink, height 0). The every-link reading is IsPositiveEvery, and IsPositiveEvery.isPositive goes from it to IsPositive given HasApexLinks.

The cone angle of a (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-circle is GX.GammaLinkCircle.coneAngle = angle f / 2 (linkCover double cover). coneAngle_eq holds for any oriented pair. coneAngle_lt_two_pi_iff states coneAngle < 2π ↔ ∀ t, f t < t + 2. It is 2π at a regular point.

To restrict a GX.SingularHSStructure to an open set use GX.SingularHSStructure.restrictTo. The inclusion U.openPartialHomeomorphSubtypeCoe is an HS-isomorphism (isIso_restrictTo). 𝔢(L) ∖ {−p̄} is GX.BiSusp.offSouth, a singular HS-surface with 𝒮 = {p̄}.

Pitfall: `h₀.relate hθ hθ' h₀'` where hθ : IsOrientedTangent p θ and the circle's pt is p only up to delta (regular p, or a `mk p …` built in the proof) can hit a whnf/isDefEq timeout, because the implicit C is unified from hθ first. Pass (C := …) explicitly and restate hθ as IsOrientedTangent C.pt θ.

Isomorphism invariance of a property of GammaLinkCircles: destructure C' and subst (kb/0085). Then use that the inverse of a (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-homeomorphism is a morphism: a private copy is in HSPositive, and TheoremMTheta has the PSL(2,ℝ) one. A generic `IsGXMorphism` of `φ.symm` lemma belongs in GX.Structure.Basic.
notes: The final `lake build GXScaffold.BBS.HSPositive` rebuilt only this module (4.0 s, nothing upstream). The file is sorry-free and warning-free under `lake env lean`; it uses only the standard axioms (checked on the main theorems with #print axioms, then removed). It imports GX.BBS.HSSuspension and GXScaffold.BBS.HSSingularities, so it graduates after HSSingularities does. It has no name clash with HSAntipodal.lean or HSDegree.lean as they stand on disk now. One follow-up becomes possible once HSAntipodal graduates: 𝔢(L) positive ⇔ L positive in the some-link reading, via GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.isIso_flip and C.antipode.IsPositive ↔ C.IsPositive. For the latter, the time-like cone angle and the light-like sign should be kept under the orientation reversal: computed by hand, not formalized. T-3p1-theorem-g can state « a positive, causal HS-sphere » as IsSingularHSSurface M A ∧ Nonempty (M ≃ₜ Sph2) ∧ A.IsPositive ∧ (causal, T-bbs-hcausal). It gets positive apex links from IsPositive, and cone angles below 2π from IsPositive.timelike / isPositive_iff_of_timelike.
